cs.t: Prefer a mouse or a trackpad, so .. maybe it's cool in a 00's way. Also, Keychron keyboards are way too heavy. Like 1 Model M too heavy. And web-based only flash updating doesn't feel like real ownership. The upside is it's a model that allows exchanging switches. One thing I didn't appreciate was red key caps without black replacements without buying a whole set.
cs.th: Keychron's Nape Pro turns your keyboard into a laptop‑style trackball rig

cs.t: I ended up switching to Keychron keyboards and found that the stabilizers do make a big difference in feel and in my own accuracy. I'm still looking for a good design that lets me put a drop-cap key where the Capslock (I've got Control there) key goes.
cs.th: Care more about the stabilizers in your mechanical keyboard–here's why

cs.t: Well some of their keyboards also hypothetically have open source firmware yet upon introducing a hardware revision they never released the necessary files. I only know this because I actually wanted to purchase one of those keyboards specifically for the open firmware. They still seem to be the best (approximately only) game in town if you want the ability to flash your own firmware to a standard off the shelf peripheral.
cs.th: Keychron announces first open-source firmware for gaming mice

cs.t: Too bad Keychron quality of late has been horrendous. Support has been abysmal too. They've gone from a beloved manufacturer to basically public enemy number 1 in the enthusiast communities.
cs.th: Keychron announces first open-source firmware for gaming mice
